# Field notes

## Eiffel Tower

The Eiffel Tower stands on the Champ de Mars in Paris. It was designed and built by the company of the engineer Gustave Eiffel for the 1889 World's Fair. The wrought-iron lattice tower is 330 metres tall and weighs about 10,100 tonnes. It was the tallest man-made structure in the world until the Chrysler Building was completed in New York in 1930.

## Photosynthesis

Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae and cyanobacteria turn light energy into chemical energy. Chlorophyll pigments in the chloroplasts absorb mostly blue and red light. Carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose, and oxygen is released as a by-product.

## Honey bees

A honey bee colony is made of a single queen, thousands of female worker bees and a few hundred male drones. Worker bees communicate the direction and distance of flowers to their sisters with the waggle dance. A strong colony can store more than 25 kilograms of honey for the winter.

## Python programming language

Python is a general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. Its design emphasises code readability through significant indentation. The reference interpreter, CPython, compiles source code to bytecode that runs on a virtual machine.

## Mount Kilimanjaro

Mount Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano in Tanzania and the highest mountain in Africa. Its summit, Uhuru Peak on the Kibo cone, reaches 5,895 metres above sea level. Its glaciers have shrunk by more than eighty percent since the early twentieth century.
